```{r setup, message = F, warning = F}
## Set chunk options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  autodep = T, # Re-run cached chunks when objects they use from other chunks change
  # Some chunks cache objects; reset them if data changes
  cache.extra = tools::md5sum(c(
    list.files(here::here("Data"), recursive = T, full.names = T),
    here::here("Helper Functions", "Analysis Functions.R")
  ))
)


## Set seed
set.seed(87204)


## Load packages
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(broom)
library(scales)
library(ggh4x)
library(mice)
library(marginaleffects)
library(tidyverse)
`%+%` <- paste0


## Load helper functions
source(here("Helper Functions", "Analysis Functions.R"))
source(here("Helper Functions", "DASS-21 Versus Norms.R"))


## Set global variables
study_period_labels <- c(
  "PIMH" = "First Study Period (2016-2019)",
  "PIH" = "Second Study Period (2019-2026)",
  "Combined" = "Combined"
)

severity_labels <- c(
  "5.5" = "Low (DASS = 5.5)",
  "8.5" = "Medium (DASS = 8.5)",
  "12"  = "High (DASS = 12)"
)

# Covariates used as moderators (3.1) and secondary predictors (3.2)
# Values: where numeric covariates are evaluated (factors: NULL, i.e., every level)
covariate_values <- list(
  age = c(20, 40, 60),
  race_recoded = NULL,
  gender = NULL,
  education = NULL,
  political_id_numeric = c(1, 4, 7), # 1-7 scale
  median_family_income = c(5, 10, 20), # In $10,000s
  dem_vote_share = c(.3, .5, .7),
  urban_rural = c(1, 4, 7, 10),
  provider_rate = c(100, 300, 500),
  referral_recoded = NULL
)

# Units for odds ratios of numeric covariates (e.g., age per 10 years); factors: 1
covariate_units <- c(
  age = 10,
  race_recoded = 1,
  gender = 1,
  education = 1,
  political_id_numeric = 1,
  median_family_income = 1, # $10,000
  dem_vote_share = .1, # 10 percentage points
  urban_rural = 1,
  provider_rate = 100, # 100 per 100,000
  referral_recoded = 1
)

covariate_labels <- c(
  age = "Age",
  race_recoded = "Race/Ethnicity",
  gender = "Gender",
  education = "Education",
  political_id_numeric = "Political Ideology",
  median_family_income = "Median Family Income (ZIP Code)",
  dem_vote_share = "Democratic Vote Share (ZIP Code)",
  urban_rural = "Urban/Rural Area (RUCA Code)",
  provider_rate = "Mental Health Providers per 100,000 (County)",
  referral_recoded = "Reason for Visiting Website"
)

covariate_value_labels <- list(
  political_id_numeric = c("Strongly Liberal", "In the Middle", "Strongly Conservative"),
  median_family_income = c("$50,000", "$100,000", "$200,000"),
  dem_vote_share = c("30%", "50%", "70%"),
  urban_rural = c("Metropolitan Core (1)", "Micropolitan Core (4)", "Small Town Core (7)", "Rural (10)")
)


## Load data
# Non-imputed datasets ("_ni")
pimh_ni <- readRDS(here("Data", "PIMH - 2012-2019", "pimh_with_geo.rds"))
pih_ni <- readRDS(here("Data", "PIH - 2019-Current", "pih_with_geo.rds"))
all_ni <- bind_rows(pimh_ni, pih_ni)

# Completed ("_c")
pimh_c <- readRDS(here("Data", "PIMH - 2012-2019", "pimh_completed.rds"))
pih_c <- readRDS(here("Data", "PIH - 2019-Current", "pih_completed.rds"))
all_c <- readRDS(here("Data", "PIMH + PIH Combined", "all_completed.rds"))
```

# 1. Sample Description

## 1.1. Sample Description Table

```{r sample-description-table}
## Variables to report
# Categorical: reported as n (%), with %s excluding missing values
categorical_vars <- c(
  "Currently self-labels as depressed" = "dep_self_label_now",
  "Race/ethnicity" = "race_recoded",
  "Gender" = "gender",
  "Education" = "education",
  "Political ideology" = "political_id",
  "Urban/rural area (RUCA code)" = "urban_rural",
  "Reason for visiting website" = "referral_recoded"
)

# Continuous: reported as mean (SD), formatted to the given accuracy
continuous_vars <- tribble(
  ~var,                   ~label,                                        ~accuracy, ~prefix,
  "depression_sum",       "DASS-21 depression sum score",                .01,       "",
  "age",                  "Age",                                         .1,        "",
  "dem_vote_share",       "Democratic vote share, ZIP code (%)",         .1,        "",
  "median_family_income", "Median family income, ZIP code (2024 $)",     1,         "$",
  "provider_rate",        "Mental health providers per 100,000, county", .1,        ""
)

ruca_labels <- c("1-3: Metropolitan", "4-6: Micropolitan", "7-9: Small Town", "10: Rural")


## Prepare data: non-imputed, with a copy of all rows labeled "Combined"
table_data <- all_ni %>%
  bind_rows(mutate(all_ni, dataset = "Combined")) %>%
  mutate(
    dataset = factor(dataset, levels = names(study_period_labels)),
    dep_self_label_now = factor(dep_self_label_now, levels = c(TRUE, FALSE), labels = c("Yes", "No")),
    urban_rural = case_when(
      between(urban_rural, 1, 3) ~ ruca_labels[1],
      between(urban_rural, 4, 6) ~ ruca_labels[2],
      between(urban_rural, 7, 9) ~ ruca_labels[3],
      urban_rural == 10 ~ ruca_labels[4]
    ) %>%
      fct(levels = ruca_labels),
    dem_vote_share = dem_vote_share * 100, # Proportion to %
    median_family_income = median_family_income * 10000 # $10,000s to $
  )


## Summarize
categorical_summary <- map2(
  .x = categorical_vars,
  .y = names(categorical_vars),
  .f = ~ summarize_categorical(table_data, var = .x, label = .y)
) %>%
  bind_rows()

continuous_summary <- pmap(
  .l = continuous_vars,
  .f = ~ summarize_continuous(table_data, var = ..1, label = ..2, accuracy = ..3, prefix = ..4)
) %>%
  bind_rows()

sample_description <- bind_rows(categorical_summary, continuous_summary) %>%
  select(row, all_of(names(study_period_labels)), is_header)


## Print
column_ns <- table_data %>% count(dataset) %>% pull(n) %>% comma()

sample_description %>%
  select(-is_header) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ replace_na(.x, ""))) %>% # Blank cells in header rows
  kable(
    col.names = c("", study_period_labels %+% "\n(N = " %+% column_ns %+% ")"),
    align = c("l", "c", "c", "c"),
    escape = F
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F) %>%
  pack_rows("Categorical variables, n (%)", 1, nrow(categorical_summary), indent = F) %>%
  pack_rows("Continuous variables, mean (SD)", nrow(categorical_summary) + 1, nrow(sample_description), indent = F) %>%
  row_spec(which(sample_description$is_header), bold = T) %>%
  add_indent(which(!sample_description$is_header & seq_len(nrow(sample_description)) <= nrow(categorical_summary)))
```

## 1.2. Depression Symptom Severity Versus Norms

Normed density plots are constructed from reported studies' summary statistics.

UK Norms (2005): Henry & Crawford (2005), Br J Clin Psychol 44:227-239

US Norms (2012): Sinclair et al. (2012), Eval Health Prof 35:259-279

```{r depression-vs-norms}
dass21_dep_compare(all_ni, depression_sum)
```

## 1.3. Trends in Outcomes

Trends in self-labeling and depressive symptom severity over time in the raw data; this is important historical context for our research questions, and it also allows us to examine the functional form of our models below.

```{r descriptive-trends}
## Observed trends in outcomes, by year (non-imputed data)
trends_by_year <- all_ni %>%
  mutate(
    study_period = fct(study_period_labels[dataset], levels = study_period_labels[c("PIMH", "PIH")]),
    `Percent Self-Labeling` = 100 * dep_self_label_now,
    `DASS-21 Depression Sum Score` = depression_sum
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    c(`Percent Self-Labeling`, `DASS-21 Depression Sum Score`),
    names_to = "measure", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  summarize(
    estimate = mean(value, na.rm = T),
    se = sd(value, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(value))),
    n = sum(!is.na(value)),
    .by = c(study_period, measure, year)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    measure = fct(measure, levels = c("Percent Self-Labeling", "DASS-21 Depression Sum Score")),
    conf.low = estimate - qnorm(.975) * se,
    conf.high = estimate + qnorm(.975) * se
  )

trends_by_year %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = estimate, color = measure)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .5) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), size = .3) +
  facet_grid(measure ~ study_period, scales = "free", space = "free_x", switch = "y") +
  facetted_pos_scales(y = list(
    measure == "Percent Self-Labeling" ~ scale_y_continuous(limits = c(20, 40), labels = label_percent(scale = 1)),
    measure == "DASS-21 Depression Sum Score" ~ scale_y_continuous(limits = c(4, 8))
  )) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2016:2026, expand = expansion(add = 0.25)) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Percent Self-Labeling" = "#2a78d6", "DASS-21 Depression Sum Score" = "#eb6834"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()
  )
```

From these plots a few things are apparent:

* There is a significant discontinuity when data collection switched from PIMH to PIH; the sample got slightly less depressed, and self-labeled less (it makes sense that these things went down together).
* Depression symptom severity in our sample matches nationwide trends in young adults; rising over time, peaking during the pandemic, and reducing afterwards.
* Depression self-labeling follows a similar trend. However, if you look closely, you can see the self-labeling trends are slightly "tilted" upwards, i.e., have a stronger slope; that is reflected in the modeling below.

These plots give us a good sense of general trends, but it's hard to examine functional form from this. These plots do a better job; they're the raw data equivalent of the model plots below.

## 1.4. Functional Form, Visually

```{r examine-functional-form}
## Self-labeling by symptom severity by year
all_ni %>%
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset, levels = c("PIMH", "PIH"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = depression_sum, y = as.numeric(dep_self_label_now), color = year, group = year)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = "y ~ x", se = F, linewidth = .7) +  
  facet_wrap(~ dataset) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(breaks = 2016:2026) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(x = "DASS-21 depression sum", y = "% currently self-labeling", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

## Self-labeling by year by symptom severity
# Create severity-banded data
banded <- all_ni %>%
  mutate(
    dataset = factor(dataset, levels = c("PIMH", "PIH")),
    severity = case_when(
      between(depression_sum, 5, 6)   ~ severity_labels[1],
      between(depression_sum, 7, 10)  ~ severity_labels[2],
      between(depression_sum, 11, 13) ~ severity_labels[3]
    ),
    severity = factor(severity, levels = severity_labels),
    dep_self_label_now = as.numeric(dep_self_label_now)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(severity))

# Summarize by year
by_year <- banded %>%
  group_by(dataset, severity, year) %>%
  summarize(x = mean(decimal_year), p = mean(dep_self_label_now), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Plot
ggplot(banded, aes(x = decimal_year, y = dep_self_label_now, color = severity)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = "y ~ x", se = F, linewidth = .7) +  
  geom_point(data = by_year, aes(x = x, y = p, size = n), alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_grid(. ~ dataset, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2016:2026, expand = expansion(add = 0.1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% currently self-labeling", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

We're looking at a largely monotonous, and perhaps linear, positive trend between year and self-labeling after conditioning for symptom severity. The years stack up more cleanly at lower levels of depressive symptom severity than at higher levels; this can be modeled with some sort of transformation on symptom severity (e.g., higher-order terms). There doesn't look to be evidence for a non-linear transformation of year.

## 1.5. Functional Form, Tested

To simplify, we will examine the functional form across the entire dataset. Robustness checks will investigate it within PIMH and PIH samples separately. In these combined models, an additional covariate, `dataset`, is added to account for the discontinuity in outcomes observed above.

### 1.5.1. Relationship Between `dep_self_label_now` and `decimal_year_centered`

As shown above, descriptively, this relationship looks approximately linear. In this chunk, we test some alternative operationalizations to assess this statistically.

```{r tff-year, cache = T}
# In PIMH
compare_models(
  pimh_c,
  list(
    "Linear" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Quadratic" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + poly(decimal_year_centered, 2) + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Cubic" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + poly(decimal_year_centered, 3) + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Log" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + log(decimal_year_centered + 6) + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Exponentiated" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + exp(decimal_year_centered) + age + race_recoded + gender + education
  )
)

# In PIH
compare_models(
  pih_c,
  list(
    "Linear" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Quadratic" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + poly(decimal_year_centered, 2) + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Cubic" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + poly(decimal_year_centered, 3) + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Log" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + log(decimal_year_centered + 6) + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Exponentiated" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + exp(decimal_year_centered) + age + race_recoded + gender + education
  )
)

# In combined data
compare_models(
  all_c,
  list(
    "Linear" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset,
    "Quadratic" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + poly(decimal_year_centered, 2) + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset,
    "Cubic" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + poly(decimal_year_centered, 3) + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset,
    "Log" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + log(decimal_year_centered + 6) + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset,
    "Exponentiated" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + exp(decimal_year_centered) + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset
  )
)
```

Indeed, all transformations fit worse, across PIMH, PIH, and combined datasets. (There is a slight improvement in BIC in the log model for PIH, but this is not indicated visually above, and results in negligible changes to point predictions and risk ratios). We conclude that this relationship is linear.

### 1.5.2. Relationship Between `dep_self_label_now` and `depression_sum`

As shown above, descriptively, this relationship is clearly "S-shaped" in all years. The question is whether this S-shape is best represented by a linear relationship on the log scale, or a transformed relationship. In this chunk, we test alternative operationalizations, then inspect them visually and by examining differences in predictions.

```{r tff-dep, cache = T}
# In PIMH
compare_models(
  pimh_c,
  list(
    "Linear" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Quadratic" = dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 2, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Cubic" = dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Log" = dep_self_label_now ~ log(depression_sum + 1) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Exponentiated" = dep_self_label_now ~ exp(depression_sum) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education
  )
)

# In PIH
compare_models(
  pih_c,
  list(
    "Linear" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Quadratic" = dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 2, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Cubic" = dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Log" = dep_self_label_now ~ log(depression_sum + 1) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education,
    "Exponentiated" = dep_self_label_now ~ exp(depression_sum) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education
  )
)

# In combined data
compare_models(
  all_c,
  list(
    "Linear" = dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset,
    "Quadratic" = dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 2, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset,
    "Cubic" = dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset,
    "Log" = dep_self_label_now ~ log(depression_sum + 1) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset,
    "Exponentiated" = dep_self_label_now ~ exp(depression_sum) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset
  )
)
```

These analyses support a cubic term in all three datasets (PIMH, PIH, combined). The addition of the cubic term slightly brings up the estimated rates of self-labeling at lower levels of symptom severity, but does not meaningfully change risk ratios by year.

### 1.5.3. Interaction Between `decimal_year_centered` and `depression_sum`

As shown above, descriptively, the relationship between year and self-labeling appears stronger at lower levels of symptom severity. This would be modeled with an interaction term; we test this here.

```{r tff-interaction, cache = T}
covariates <- " + age + race_recoded + gender + education"

# In PIMH
tff_interaction_pimh <- compare_models(
  pimh_c,
  list(
    "Best-Fit" = "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered" %+% covariates,
    "Interaction" = "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) * decimal_year_centered" %+% covariates
  )
)

# In PIH
tff_interaction_pih <- compare_models(
  pih_c,
  list(
    "Best-Fit" = "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered" %+% covariates,
    "Interaction" = "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) * decimal_year_centered" %+% covariates
  )
)

# In combined data, allowing the severity curve to differ by study period, so the interaction is not confounded with the change between study periods
tff_interaction_all <- compare_models(
  all_c,
  list(
    "Best-Fit" = "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered" %+% covariates %+% " + dataset + poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE):dataset",
    "Interaction" = "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) * decimal_year_centered" %+% covariates %+% " + dataset + poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE):dataset"
  )
)

# Severity x year terms (log-odds) and p-values
list(PIMH = tff_interaction_pimh, PIH = tff_interaction_pih, Combined = tff_interaction_all) %>%
  map("coefficients") %>%
  bind_rows(.id = "dataset") %>%
  filter(model == "Interaction", str_detect(term, ":decimal_year_centered")) %>%
  select(-model) %>%
  show_table(digits = 6)
```

The interaction term improves model fit in the combined data, but not in either dataset individually. If effects of `depression_sum` on `dep_self_label_now` are larger in earlier years in the combined data, this is likely an artifact of the two datasets; this trend does not appear in either dataset individually.

These analyses pretty conclusively support a best-fit model of `dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education`. This section does not examine the functional form of covariates to the outcome; for the sake of parsimony in primary analyses, this is assumed to be linear. These relationships are investigated further in secondary analyses.

# 2. Primary Analysis

The preregistered primary analysis model is `dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education`.

Per the above analyses, the functional form is better represented by the function `dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education`.

For the primary analysis, we use the best-fit functions above. We report findings from simpler, preregistered models in `Robustness Checks/Preregistered Models.Rmd`.

## 2.1. Primary Regression Results

```{r primary-regressions, cache = T}
# Save baseline model formulas
pimh_model_base <- "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education"
pih_model_base <- "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education"
all_model_base <- "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset"

# Fit primary models, keeping results only
primary <- list(
  PIMH = summarize_fit(pimh_c, pimh_model_base, years = 2016:2019),
  PIH = summarize_fit(pih_c, pih_model_base, years = 2019:2026),
  Combined = summarize_fit(all_c, all_model_base, years = c(2016, 2026), plots = T) # Combined, best-fit (i.e., incorporates above considerations)
)

# PIMH
show_table(odds_ratios(primary$PIMH$coefficients))
show_table(primary$PIMH$predictions)
show_table(primary$PIMH$ratios)

# PIH
show_table(odds_ratios(primary$PIH$coefficients))
show_table(primary$PIH$predictions)
show_table(primary$PIH$ratios)

# Combined
show_table(odds_ratios(primary$Combined$coefficients))
show_table(primary$Combined$predictions)
show_table(primary$Combined$ratios)
```

## 2.2. Primary Regression Results, Visualized

For the sake of parsimony, and because results do not differ meaningfully between datasets, results will be visualized using the combined model.

```{r primary-regressions-visualized}
plot_trend(primary$Combined$trend)
plot_curve(primary$Combined$curve)
```

# 3. Secondary Analyses

## 3.1. Moderation of Primary Analyses

```{r moderation, cache = T}
# Each covariate's interaction with year is added to the primary model, in each dataset
# Combined data: the covariate's effect may also differ by study period (covariate:dataset), so moderation is not confounded with the change between study periods
# Reason for visiting was asked in PIH only; gender is tested in PIH only (no TGD participants in PIMH)
# Fit moderation models, keeping results only; plot data for the combined data only
moderation <- expand_grid(
  dataset = c("PIMH", "PIH", "Combined"),
  moderator = names(covariate_values)
) %>%
  filter(!moderator %in% c("referral_recoded", "gender") | dataset == "PIH") %>%
  mutate(
    data = list(PIMH = pimh_c, PIH = pih_c, Combined = all_c)[dataset],
    base = c(PIMH = pimh_model_base, PIH = pih_model_base, Combined = all_model_base)[dataset],
    base = if_else(dataset == "Combined", base %+% " + dataset:" %+% moderator, base),
    results = pmap(
      list(data, base, moderator, dataset),
      ~ fit_moderation(..1, ..2, ..3, covariate_values[[..3]], covariate_units[[..3]], plots = ..4 == "Combined")
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-data)

# Moderator x year odds ratios (per unit of numeric moderators), with Benjamini-Hochberg correction within each dataset
moderation %>%
  mutate(coefficients = map(results, "coefficients")) %>%
  select(dataset, coefficients) %>%
  unnest(coefficients) %>%
  mutate(p.adjusted = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"), .by = dataset) %>%
  show_table()

# Risk ratios per year by moderator value, at DASS = 8.5
moderation %>%
  mutate(ratios = map(results, "ratios")) %>%
  select(dataset, moderator, ratios) %>%
  unnest(ratios) %>%
  select(dataset, moderator, value, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value) %>%
  show_table()

# Visualized, combined data
moderation %>%
  filter(dataset == "Combined") %>%
  pwalk(function(moderator, results, ...) {
    title <- covariate_labels[[moderator]]
    trend <- label_groups(results$trend, moderator, covariate_values[[moderator]], covariate_value_labels[[moderator]])
    curve <- label_groups(results$curve, moderator, covariate_values[[moderator]], covariate_value_labels[[moderator]])
    print(plot_trend(trend, title = title))
    print(plot_curve(curve, title = title))
  })
```

## 3.2. Concept Breadth by Participant Characteristics

```{r cb-by-char, cache = T}
# Baseline model for these tests
secondary_base <- "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3, raw = TRUE)"

# Fit each model, keeping results only (numeric covariates: risk ratio = highest vs. lowest value)
secondary <- imap(covariate_values, ~ fit_secondary(pih_c, secondary_base, .y, .x, covariate_units[[.y]]))

# Covariate odds ratios (per unit of numeric covariates), with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all terms
map(secondary, "coefficients") %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(p.adjusted = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) %>%
  show_table()

# Risk ratios between levels of each covariate, at DASS = 8.5
map(secondary, "ratios") %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  select(term, contrast, depression_sum, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value) %>%
  show_table()

# Visualized
iwalk(
  secondary,
  ~ label_groups(.x$curve, .y, covariate_values[[.y]], covariate_value_labels[[.y]]) %>%
    plot_curve_by(label = covariate_labels[[.y]]) %>%
    print()
)
```

# 4. Robustness Checks

Robustness checks are reported in the folder `Robustness Checks/`. They include:

* Primary analyses using simple preregistered models
* Primary analyses using complete cases
* Primary analyses controlling for `referral_recoded`
* Robustness checks around age findings, including:
  * Age findings, controlling for `referral_recoded` or other potential confounders
  * Age findings, binned (18-22, 25+)
